summary: Observation of the evolution of two circular shapes
description: On December 25, 1993, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness driving on the highway observed two circular shapes, estimated to be about 1 meter in diameter, flame-red in color, above a canal at an altitude of approximately 4 and 6 meters. The objects then separated; one sped off, while the second continued moving at a reduced speed, and the witness was able to follow it along the highway, where he was driving at approximately 140 km/h. As the second object was faster, the witness lost sight of it. No noise was heard, and the duration of the observation was not recorded. The investigation led to the discovery of a second witness, but the previous day at a different time, and it cannot be confirmed that this was the same phenomenon. This phenomenon has not been identified.

summary: Observation of light effects from a disco projector
description: Three members of the same family witnessed cylindrical luminous phenomena in the sky between 1:45 a.m. and 3:00 a.m. on the night of December 10-11, 1993. The investigation focused on the use of a Sky Rose laser, which was operating between 10:30 p.m. and 3:00 a.m. on the roof of a nightclub.

summary: Observation of a large light spinning around in the sky with erratic movements: probable observation of a laser.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named PRIVAS (07) 1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 11, 1993, at approximately 8:50 PM, a motorist was intrigued by a very large light that rotated in the sky and then disappeared. A little further on, the light reappeared, and the two passengers in the vehicle also observed this phenomenon. Upon arriving in a parking lot, the witness pointed out the UFO to another driver. The witness reported that for about twenty minutes, this light rotated silently on its axis. Several other lights (between six and ten) were observed below it. The UFO appeared and disappeared, moving forward while spinning in all directions. Only one witness reported their observation to the Gendarmerie. The description has the characteristics found in a laser animation observation originating from the ground and reflected in the atmosphere (due to moisture droplets or cloud cover): patterns in the sky with one or more points or segments of light, in one or more colors, according to a fixed or, more often, variable geometry; rotation, scanning, and pivoting of the patterns, with the possibility of large and rapid excursions across the sky. Depending on atmospheric conditions, beams rising from the ground may or may not be visible (as is the case here; sometimes only the upward beams are visible without projecting patterns in the sky). Laser displays, now frequent and easily recognizable in GEIPAN reports, were rarer in 1993. It is not currently possible to investigate the origin of this display at the location or its vicinity (near Avignon). However, we have an observation this year, by chance on the same day but in a completely different location, where the investigation allowed us to trace the activity and revealed that the equipment producing such effects was sold to nightclubs in France (see the police report for the observation case ILE BOUCHARD (37) 11.12.1993). GEIPAN classifies the observation case as B: probable (and not certain, due to the inability to identify the installation or verify the compatibility of the weather conditions) laser or "Sky Rose" observation.

summary: Observation of a stationary yellow ball
description: On November 26, between 7:15 and 8:15 a.m., a witness observed a yellow sphere that appeared to be burning for nearly an hour. After an hour, the sphere quickly disappeared, leaving behind a black trail. The investigation failed to identify the sphere as a civilian or military aircraft, nor as a balloon. The phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of violent flashes
description: During the night of November 22nd to 23rd, between 5:30 and 7:00 AM, two witnesses observed very intense flashes of light seven times through their closed shutters. No further information is available.

summary: Observation of a bright streak surrounded by bright dots: lack of information.
description: On the night of November 16-17, 1993, at approximately 12:45 a.m., a witness observed a steady, luminous streak in the sky, "like a neon tube," around which several other points of light rotated. This phenomenon was accompanied by a faint noise, reminiscent of a small airplane. The witness woke his friend, who was also able to observe the phenomenon. Despite a newspaper article, no further information has been gathered.

summary: Observation of a circle of lights of varying colors and light intensity moving silently: unexplained phenomenon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named ECQUEVILLY (78) 15.11.1993, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. During the night of November 14-15, 1993, at around 4:30 a.m., a witness was awakened by the barking of his dogs. He got up and confirmed that his dogs, as well as his horses, were all looking in the same direction. The witness went to another room in the house and, through the window (approximately 300 meters west of his home, according to the police), saw stationary lights illuminating the ground. The witness heard no noise, even with the window open. However, he noticed the lights moving towards him. When they reached the roof of his house, the witness saw a luminous circle composed of white, yellow, and slightly bluish lights of varying intensities. Flashes of black light were also observed. The observation lasted between 20 and 25 seconds. The witness left his home, but the lights had disappeared. The witness went to the police station on November 24, 1993, to give his statement and later submitted sketches of his observations. No trace of the lights was found, and no other witness statements were collected during the police investigation. GEIPAN contacted the witness again in July 2018. Our analysis (see the investigation report) has shown that the UFO observed by the witness was ultimately of a relatively modest size (approximately 5th at its closest point). This modest size contrasts with the sketches made by the witness, which suggested that the UFO could have been larger. However, this angular size remains too large to fit well with the only somewhat credible hypothesis: that of confusion with a helicopter. Indeed, this hypothesis would imply that the helicopter was close to the witness (approximately 55 meters for a helicopter of the EC145 type at the time), and was therefore heard, in a context of nighttime silence, with the window open, whereas the witness heard no noise. Other testimonial parameters also prevent us from validating this hypothesis, such as the large number of lights observed, the absence of navigation and anti-collision lights, and the ground illumination provided by a black light. The consistency is good, with a sufficiently detailed testimony and an on-site investigation carried out shortly afterward by the gendarmes. Although the witness did not think to take photos and videos, and no angular measurements were taken during the investigation by the gendarmes, we were nevertheless able, thanks in particular to the photographs taken on-site by the gendarmes, the sketch, and the witness's testimony, to accurately reconstruct the trajectory of the UFO and visualize its appearance. In the current GEIPAN methodology, the present level of strangeness and consistency necessitates conducting a field investigation with the witness for reconstruction and cognitive interviewing. This last factor is likely to positively and negatively impact the assessment of both strangeness and consistency. However, it is not possible for a case revisited so long afterward. Therefore, the evaluation of the present case is carried out according to the current criteria for taking strangeness and consistency into account (see the GEIPAN news item of April 27, 2017 The classification methodology at GEIPAN) as if the field investigation had been conducted and had been completely neutral (no additional or subtracted information), which is sometimes the case. However, to highlight this methodological difference, the classification is based on ABCD and not on the current ABC D1/D2 system, which, for the unexplained classification, corresponds to a stronger validation of the unexplained nature of the case. Here, the case is on the borderline between an unexplained case and one that cannot be investigated due to a lack of consistency in the case file, resulting from the absence of an on-site GEIPAN investigation. Consequently, the case is classified as D: unexplained.

summary: Observations on several occasions of traces on the ground of different shapes and sizes: unusable as it exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named NOEUX-LES-MINES (62) 30.10.1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On three occasions, over a period of about two weeks in early November 1993, the owners (T1 and T2) of a house found traces of flattened and crushed grass in their garden: a first winding line approximately 8 meters long and 40 cm wide, then a second line about ten meters long, and finally a circle at the junction of the two lines. They had these different traces documented by a neighbor (T3). T1 stated that between November 8th and 14th, around 1:00 AM, she had seen a yellowish light moving at a height of 0.60 meters above the ground. T3 also noted that her dogs had been barking abnormally for about two weeks around 1:30 AM. The witnesses filed their statements late, and the gendarmerie went to the site on November 17, 1993. The observation concerned ground marks, not any aerospace phenomenon. Indeed, the observation by T2 telescope (and only by T2 telescope) of a "yellowish light at a height of 60 cm moving around around 1:00 AM" is not related to the marks. It was seen after the marks had been detected and is not unusual in itself; in particular, its position in the photograph does not allow the witness to determine whether this light was above their property or much further away on other properties. This light would probably not have been reported if the marks had not already caused concern among the witnesses. It is not within GEIPAN's remit (and therefore not within its area of expertise) to investigate the explanation of ground traces in the absence of evidence of an aerospace phenomenon coinciding with their discovery. Indeed, suspicious ground traces can have a wide variety of origins unrelated to UAPs. A few examples (without claiming they are all relevant here) include: mushrooms, thieves, wild or domestic animals, or neighborly pranks or amusements. GEIPAN would not have been able to classify this case as a Category D UAP because nothing indicates that it is an aerospace phenomenon, given the information gathered. In conclusion, GEIPAN is reclassifying this case as Category C: unusable because it falls outside GEIPAN's sole area of expertise.

summary: Observation of a luminous halo passing over a surveillance camera
description: On October 21, 1993, at approximately 9:00 PM, a security guard at a company observed a halo of light, containing a very bright hemisphere, on his surveillance camera for several minutes. The phenomenon moved slowly across the camera's field of view before disappearing behind the trees. It is possible that it was the observation of car headlights, but no evidence could be found to support this hypothesis.

summary: Observations of multicolored lights in a clearing followed by a loud noise and a violent flash: thunderstorm.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named BESSINES SUR GARTEMPE (87) 1993, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 5, 1993, at approximately 6:20 PM, several people in a garden near a wood observed colored lights appearing in a clearing. After a few moments, the witnesses heard a sound like thunder and saw a flash of lightning. The luminous phenomenon in the clearing disappeared. Re-examining this case allows us to establish the following points: - the witnesses' descriptions use terms usually associated with thunderstorm events: lightning, thunder, detonation; - the arguments against a thunderstorm explanation are unconvincing. "It wasn't a thunderstorm because... there wouldn't have been a single detonation," "the lightning flashes went in one direction and the detonation or noise in the other." - the element that seemed the strangest, the glimmers in the woods, did not lead to verification by the witnesses that they were indeed coming from the woods, because the witnesses gave up trying to investigate. Therefore, it could very well have been a series of lightning flashes seen through the woods. Indeed, the observation site (near the vegetable garden) is located on the southern side of a hill (Puy de Sarran). The lights are seen at the northernmost clearing, which is near the summit of Puy de Sarran. The wooded areas are mostly on the sides of this hill (the downward slope is 10 by 70 m), so that flashes from the northern or northwestern horizon of the hill (no trees on the eastern side of the hill) can be seen through the trees without passing through much tree cover (the wooded area is shaped like a hill) to appear on the surface of the clearing (this is seen from a witness and therefore without obstruction from trees). The fact that the lights were seen 4 meters above the ground at the level of the clearing further reduces the thickness of the trees traversed upstream of the clearing by the lightning's path. - The Limoges weather service, contacted by the brigade by mail regarding the situation at 6:00 PM, and without providing any context, indicated nothing abnormal at 6:00 PM without extending the timeframe. However, the response from the Sauvagnac radio station reported heavy rain, distant thunderstorms, and lightning in several directions, starting at 8:00 PM, without specifying the timeframe from 6:30 PM to 7:00 PM. This information is highly consistent with the occurrence of thunderstorm warnings (a few flashes of lightning and a single clap of thunder) 30 minutes to an hour earlier, 12 km further north. - The witnesses are friends, seemingly in a rather cheerful or lively mood (each having drunk three beers and a pastis in the afternoon before the observation (see report)), it's possible this facilitated communication and even amplified the feeling of strangeness. - It might be surprising that the police didn't notice the storm from their station, located 2 km from the observation site. The lightning may have been masked by the terrain, since the hypothesis is that the lightning was distant and beyond the mountain range, and in any case, lightning isn't always seen indoors. On the other hand, the detonating sound ("like an explosion or a clap of thunder") was indeed heard from T4's home, but this is located closer to the garden (1 km) and north of the mountain range, therefore closer to the presumed origin of the thunder and without any potential sound barrier created by the mountain range. It is not possible to definitively state that the origin of the UFOs is the thunderstorm, but all the evidence suggests this hypothesis has a probability greater than 50%. Furthermore, the consistency of the eyewitness accounts is weakened by the complete lack of angular measurements of the origins and durations of the flashes. The accounts as a whole are virtually unusable. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: thunderstorm.

summary: Observation of luminous points forming 2 identical isosceles triangles.
description: On April 24, 2008, a person reported an observation made during the summer of 1993 to 1997 (the witness did not recall the exact date, and the given date was arbitrary). The witness, along with five other people, observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in a clear sky between 9:00 and 10:00 PM. Points forming two isosceles triangles appeared to be rotating around the central axis of each triangle. Suddenly, these points ceased their movement, and the triangles moved in opposite directions: the first, heading towards Mont Gros, disappeared, hidden by the landscape; the second initially stopped above the sea before resuming its rotation and vanishing abruptly. It is very difficult, if not impossible, to investigate such a late testimony (reported on April 24, 2008). We frequently observe flying triangles; some remain unexplained, but many others are simply mistaken for airplanes seen from a particular angle. In this case, we have too little information to confirm the airplane hypothesis at this time.

summary: Observation of a circle of flattened grass in the garden of a pavilion.
description: On September 27, 1993, the owner of a house noticed a regular circle, approximately 8 meters in diameter, in his yard. Around the perimeter, the grass was flattened outwards to a width of 30 cm. An automatic sprinkler nozzle was located in the center of the circle. It should be noted that a violent storm had flooded the property in the preceding days, and that electrical disturbances had occurred during this storm, specifically affecting the fuse that powers the automatic sprinkler system. A quick analysis by SEPRA (the French Society of Electrical and Electronic Systems) led to the hypothesis that the sprinkler nozzle had opened unexpectedly, resulting in watering without pressure for a period of time, which caused the observed phenomenon.

summary: Observation of an elongated light passing at high speed
description: On the night of September 27-28, 1993, around midnight, a witness briefly observed an intense, elongated light that passed by at high speed and without noise. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Likely sighting of disco lights
description: On the night of September 11-12, 1993, numerous witnesses reported seeing many bright lights forming an undefined shape and rotating in the sky. The investigation revealed that these were likely spotlights from a nearby nightclub.

summary: Observation of a bright orange point changing shape: lack of information.
description: On the night of September 4-5, 1993, around midnight, four witnesses in their vehicle observed a bright orange light, larger than a star, moving like an airplane as it approached. The observation lasted two to three minutes, during which the object abruptly changed shape, becoming a very elongated diamond or a cigar shape. No sound was heard. No other information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of lights created by laser projectors at a funfair
description: On October 6, 1993, at approximately 10:30 PM, numerous witnesses observed a circular luminous phenomenon composed of several luminous spheres. The investigation revealed it to be a ride equipped with rotating laser projectors.

summary: Several paragliders likely to be observed in flight
description: On August 21, 1993, at approximately 3:45 PM, two witnesses observed bright points of different colors in the very clear sky, moving very slowly. As one witness specified, the observation was likely that of paragliders in flight.

summary: Observation of a luminous triangle
description: On August 19, 1993, at approximately 10:00 PM, a witness on their terrace observed a bright object very high in the sky with three white lights. The observation lasted about a minute; no sound was detected. No other information is available.

summary: A low-flying aircraft is likely to pass overhead.
description: On August 19, 1993, around 6:00 a.m., the police received several calls reporting a very loud and unusual noise, a flash of light, and an explosion. The on-site investigation yielded nothing, but it appeared to have been caused by a low-flying aircraft.

summary: Observation of an elliptical shape moving slowly across the sky
description: On August 18, 1993, at approximately 2:30 a.m., a witness observed an elliptical luminous phenomenon, delimited by several light sources, moving slowly and silently across the sky. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of white light emanating from an aircraft during landing
description: On August 17, 1993, at approximately 11:00 PM, two witnesses observed two white lights and flashing red lights moving slowly without any audible noise. The investigation quickly revealed that a DC-8 military aircraft arriving from England that evening was searching for the runway and had made wide turns in the area. The observed headlights and lights corresponded to the aircraft's navigational aids.

summary: Observations from several locations of a stationary red luminous phenomenon in the direction of the Pyrenees; rapid disappearance: unusable as it exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named SAINT-GAUDENS (31) 14.08.1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On Saturday, August 14, 1993, around 10:00 PM, several people in two different locations observed an unusual phenomenon in the direction of the Pyrenees. Three witnesses reported their observations to the Gendarmerie. The described phenomenon is a circular, red, stationary point of light to the right of Mont Valier (for T1 and T3) and in the direction of Cagire (for T2). One of the witnesses (T3) uses binoculars and observes five red-orange points of light within the object. The observations last approximately 10 minutes, then the point disappears in a few seconds. T2's entire oral account is perfectly consistent with a phenomenon that would only occur on the ground. Indeed, it is seen in the woods at the start and then moving into the Pyrenees mountain range, in a horizontal motion. It is worth considering whether this is also the case for the other testimonies, in which case the search for an explanation would exceed the sole competence of GEIPAN. T1 and T3, whose observation points are close, place the UFO, based on their statements or drawings, at the level of Mont Valier, slightly to the right. Only T3 mentions the sky at the end of his observation, with the phrase "the strange phenomenon disappeared horizontally in the sky." This does not mean that the UFO was in the open sky. Mont Valier is not an isolated peak and extends to its right with a ridge line visible at a slightly lower angular height, as seen from the observation point (Saint-Gaudens). Moreover, several landforms are visible in the foreground of Mont Valier, also at the same angular height to the right. The mountain range at the summit of Cournudere (1563 m) is particularly noteworthy. The drawings of T1 and T3 may depict one of these successive landform lines, but certainly not the horizon line, which T1 and T3 may not even have noticed. - T2 and T3 orally describe a disappearance along the horizontal path (the object disappeared while disappearing into the Pyrenees mountain range, in a horizontal movement). However, the drawings of T1 and T2, taken alone without knowledge of the mention of a horizontal movement, could suggest an ascent in altitude. The oral mention of a horizontal movement cannot in any way apply to a UFO that would have been seen with increasing angular elevation. It must therefore be understood that witnesses T2 and T3 wanted to represent in their drawings a horizontal movement that primarily involves a change in distance. This cannot be directly translated into a flat drawing, so the two witnesses represent it in perspective with a circle showing the UFO's increasingly smaller size. They wanted to represent a disappearance in distance and not an ascent in altitude. This disappearance in distance may only be an illusion. Indeed, some witnesses perceiving a decrease in the brightness of a UAPs, whose actual distance they cannot assess, may interpret this as an effective decrease in the light emitted by the UAP, which would be stationary, or as a receding distance from a UAP whose light would be constant. The GEIPAN experiment shows that the context of experienced strangeness very often leads the witness to interpret it as receding when the UAP is actually stationary. T1's testimony introduces a form of inconsistency that is more difficult to overcome. T1 does not orally describe any movement of the UAP, including during its disappearance. The forward tilt associated with the appearance of three beams of light can only be understood as a perception of a change in the UAP's orientation, since it was already perceived with an oriented shape (e.g., a flattened ovoid shape). The main drawing is consistent with the account, showing a fixed point (no angular evolution). However, the secondary drawing mentions a change of course. with an upward arrow. In this context, one might think that T1 also wanted to express, in perspective, a flight in distance, but the inconsistency prevents us from drawing a conclusion. The search for an explanation therefore exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN since the observation, once the unusable part of T1's testimony is set aside, is consistent with a phenomenon entirely located on the ground. GEIPAN at the time would not have classified this case as Category D, because nothing indicates that it is an Aerospace Phenomenon. Nevertheless, GEIPAN can provide some clues to search for a ground-based phenomenon, without being able to claim to circumscribe the search area (see the investigation report). But this search is hampered by the fact that the observation direction of T2, as indicated by the Pic de Cagire, does not intersect those of T1 and T3, reported as being to the right of Mont Valier, except in the hypothesis T2 would have designated the Pic de Cagire as the reference point instead of Mont Valier. Nothing allows us to confirm or refute such a confusion. The angular difference between the two peaks is admittedly small (20°), but for a witness familiar with the area, the two landmarks are quite distinct, even at night. A more thorough investigation at the time would have made it possible to identify this difference, seek more precise information from the witnesses, and either resolve or confirm this discrepancy. At this stage, this discrepancy adds to the strangeness because the correspondence in appearance, time, and duration would suggest a phenomenon of the same nature that would therefore have occurred in two different locations. A lack of explanation at the end of an investigation that would also utilize all the skills required for investigating ground phenomena (and not just aerospace phenomena) would, in turn, create a higher standard for the consistency of the testimonies (level of information and evaluation of its reliability). that there is little chance of success 25 years after the events, thus leading to unusable evidence rather than simply unexplained circumstances. Consequently, the case is classified as Class C: unusable because it exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN.

summary: Observation for a few minutes of a triangular shape
description: On August 13, 1993, at approximately 9:00 AM, a witness observed a stationary, triangular-shaped object from his home. The observation lasted only a few minutes and had disappeared by the time the witness returned with his camcorder to try and film it. No aerial phenomena occurred in that area that day, and no further information could be gathered.

summary: Observations of a bright yellow phenomenon lasting about twenty minutes in the night sky: very likely observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named VIGY (57) 1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On August 11, 1993, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a witness (T1) driving his car observed a very bright yellow light stationary above a farm and then the Hayes castle. The witness described a large, luminous sphere rotating silently, larger than a star. The shape subsequently described was that of a disc surmounted by a dome, or an inverted mushroom. The light intensity gradually decreased, and the UFO appeared to move away in the direction of Charleville-sous-Bois. Upon returning home, the witness asked his mother (T2) to observe the phenomenon. Climbing onto a chair, she saw a uniform yellow light, fixed in the starry sky, then quickly went back to bed. T1 observed the UFO until its complete disappearance. The total observation time for T1 was 20 minutes. The data, combined with the geographical location indicating an observation towards the Northeast, suggests a possible confusion with the planet Venus, which also rises in the Northeast (Azimuth 58°): Positional correlation: - the first observation by T1 (from Le Marais to Ferme St Leon) corresponds to an azimuth of 62°, the second (from Ferme St Leon to Cheteau de Hayes) to 56°. The sighting by T2 is less precise because it indicates the forest of Charleville-sous-Bois; the azimuth of the forested area around Charleville-sous-Bois is between 38° and 62°. - the UFO is low in the sky, like Venus. T2 obtained the visibility of the UFO above the forest (e I saw a very bright light in the sky just above the forest of Charleville-sous-Bois e) by standing on a chair. This means that the UFO and the forest are close enough angularly to clear the view together above a nearby obstacle due to a small gain in the angular field of view (standing on a 50 cm chair allows a gain of 0.6 arcseconds for an obstacle at 50 m and 3 arcseconds for an obstacle at 10 m). Visibility of Venus: - T2's readings indicate that, in the direction of observation, the sky was showing stars. - We verified that there were no ground obstacles preventing Venus from being visible despite its low altitude in the sky (at least 3 arcseconds at the start of the observation). Angular Stationarity of the UFO: The stationarity of the UFO noted by both witnesses (and over a period of 20 minutes for T1) also supports the hypothesis of a celestial body. Witness 1's mention of the impression of the UFO moving towards Charleville-sous-Bois (i.e., along the line of sight) is subjective and linked to its decrease in brightness, which the witness also mentions. The variation in intensity results from a change in atmospheric thickness or the appearance of cloud cover. The witness who does not recognize Venus logically interprets the decrease in intensity as the UFO moving away. The disappearance of the UFO, observed only by T1, is perceived as the culmination of the reduced intensity and the distance. Appearance: The initial shape described by T1, a large, luminous yellow ball, is a typical misidentification of Venus. This celestial body is brighter than the stars (its high intensity gives the impression of a luminous sphere), and colors are introduced by the thick atmosphere, as the celestial body is seen here at a low altitude in the sky (3rd). The description of an elongated shape with a central dome or an inverted mushroom shape is more difficult to explain, but since Venus is very low on the horizon (3rd), it is possible that atmospheric turbulence distorts its image. The appearance of cloud cover could also cause the light from Venus to be scattered. It is indeed noted that for T1, this shape (other than the initial spherical shape) is only distinguishable at a later stage, and that for T2, who only observed sporadically and later, the light was inside the UFO (This light was yellow, like the color of car headlights. It was uniform. What I saw was an object illuminated by itself). The above elements indicate a very strong coincidence with an observation of Venus. Only the description of the shape in the second part of the observation is somewhat more unusual compared to the mass of misinterpretations recorded with Venus at GEIPAN. But it is not unique; it can be explained and therefore cannot call into question the highly probable nature of the Venus hypothesis. The consistency is average; both witnesses filed reports with the Gendarmerie, but their testimonies lack direct and precise assessments (elevation, azimuth). There is a certain inconsistency in the T2 report, which notes the strange nature of the object ("This is the first time I've observed similar phenomena"), particularly after a very precise description of its shape, but then stops the observation (after 5 or 7 minutes) before the UFO disappeared. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: highly probable sightings of Venus.

summary: OBJECT THE SIZE OF A HOT AIR BALLOON
description: On August 8, 1993, witnesses observed a spherical light, about the size of a hot air balloon, around 10 PM. The observation lasted 30 seconds, then the object quickly disappeared with a high-pitched whistling sound. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a bright flash and a black object disappearing very quickly with a whistling sound
description: On August 7th, at 10:45 PM, a witness driving his car observed a large, very intense, stationary white light for about a minute. When the light disappeared, a whistling sound was heard, and a black shape appeared to vanish at very high speed. The following day, the witness experienced muscle pain, and upon returning to the site, he suffered severe headaches at the location of the observation. The investigation revealed that there was no air traffic in the area, and the phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Probable observation of a celestial body
description: On August 7, 1993, around 5:00 AM, three witnesses leaving a nightclub observed a very bright point in the sky. The shape was indistinct according to the witnesses (round or triangular), but it remained stationary. The bright point gradually faded with sunrise and disappeared. The witnesses likely observed a very bright celestial object.

summary: Circle of wheat stalks in a field
description: On July 25, 1993, a farmer harvesting his field discovered a circle of flattened wheat. No formal explanation has been found for this observation, although neighborhood inquiries strongly suggest the possibility of human intervention, perhaps by neighbors.

summary: observation by three witnesses of a luminous object appearing to rotate on itself.
description: During the night of July 24-25, 1993, between 2:45 and 3:30 a.m., three witnesses observed a white light phenomenon that moved and rotated, displaying numerous points of light. The investigation quickly revealed that it was a multi-faceted spotlight from a nearby nightclub, its light reflecting off the low cloud ceiling and visible from a great distance. The nightclub manager, when questioned, confirmed this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of luminous halos
description: On January 23, 1993, at approximately 12:20 AM, a witness observed five luminous halos in the cloudy sky from their window. Each halo, with an apparent diameter of 1.5 meters, rotated relative to one another, maintaining a constant distance. The witness's mother also observed the phenomenon. After a short time, one of the halos disappeared very quickly, while the others continued to rotate. The phenomenon remained silent and was observed for about 15 minutes. The hypothesis of distant spotlights was favored.

summary: Observation of a test advertising projector
description: On July 21, 1993, at approximately 12:30 a.m., six people reported seeing numerous luminous orbs swirling in the sky and sweeping across the horizon. An investigation revealed that the phenomenon originated from a projector being tested in the parking lot of a nearby nightclub. This type of projector emits 30 rotating beams that sweep across the horizon.

summary: Observation of luminous circles, probably originating from spotlights or laser beams
description: During the night of July 17-18, 1993, between 12:30 a.m. and 2:30 a.m., a witness observed a series of bright white circles rotating rapidly in the sky from their home. After about an hour, a third circle joined the other two. The witness ceased observing this phenomenon around 2:30 a.m. While not proven, it is highly probable that the observed phenomenon was a beam from advertising spotlights or laser beams, perhaps from a nightclub.

summary: Observations on three occasions of the movement of luminous colored phenomena in the night sky: probable observations of airliners.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named MAUVEZIN (32) 1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On July 15, 1993, around 11:00 PM, and then again on the 16th around 1:00 AM and 2:00 AM, three young campers, seasonal workers in Mauvezin (32), observed colored luminous phenomena moving across the sky on three separate occasions. Witnesses reported hearing a muffled noise during some sightings. One witness attempted to take photographs, but the results proved unusable. The most plausible explanation for this series of sightings is that of aircraft misidentification, which exhibits characteristics identical to those of aircraft approaching or having just taken off from Toulouse-Blagnac Airport. We note in particular: - the presence of powerful white/yellow lights, similar to landing lights, illuminated during approach or takeoff; - the presence of a red light described as central, similar to one of the anti-collision lights, located under the fuselage, although flashing was not mentioned in the witness statements. - The shape described by witnesses can be quite similar to that defined by an aircraft's landing lights, either an equilateral triangle when the UFO is observed from below, or another geometric shape depending on the angle of observation. - The movement of the UFOs is identical to the R17 air corridor on a heading of 304°E, connecting Toulouse-Blagnac Airport to point AGN114.8 Ch95X. Even if this route was not the same in 1993 as it is today, the relative proximity of Toulouse-Blagnac Airport does not preclude overflights of the area where the witnesses were located, or the presence of nearby airliners on approach or shortly after takeoff. - The mention of a noise emanating from the UFO in two of the three phases, a noise whose intensity and nature can vary considerably depending on the environment (weather, particularly wind, terrain) and the distance of the UFO from the witness. The fact that the witnesses are student seasonal workers living far from the observation site and unfamiliar with proximity to an air corridor, at least this one, may explain the confusion with aircraft and the absence of other testimonies. The consistency is average. Although all the witnesses were interviewed at the Gendarmerie and the resulting report is fairly complete, it lacks important data such as azimuth readings and elevation angles of the UFOs. An on-site investigation would have clarified many points and potentially confirmed the hypothesis, had the flights suspected of causing the confusion been located at the time. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable sightings of airliners.

summary: A disco projector was likely to be spotted during the national holiday.
description: During the night of July 13-14, 1993, around 1:30 a.m., a witness observed a white circular shape rotating and splitting in two for about fifteen minutes. No other witnesses were found, but given the date of the observation and the numerous festivities organized for the occasion, the observation of a nightclub projector or laser beam is likely.

summary: Periodic observation for 1 hour and 30 minutes of a rotating white luminous shape. Probable laser beam from a nightclub.
description: On July 10, 1993, around 1:00 AM, a witness observed a light without a clearly defined shape, rotating clockwise with a slight buzzing sound. Intrigued, the witness went to get his friend, who was also observing the phenomenon, and in turn, he woke his mother, who was also able to see it. Two other witnesses were located by the police but declined to comment. The phenomenon reappeared approximately every 20 minutes until 2:30 AM, at which time the witnesses decided to go to bed. The phenomenon has not been formally identified, but it is likely that it was the observation of a laser beam from a nightclub about 10 km away, given the cloud cover present that day and the line of sight.

summary: Observation of red luminous points accompanied by noise
description: On July 8, 1993, around midnight, a taxi driver and his passenger, returning from the train station, observed red lights through the windshield. After stopping the car, the driver got out, but the lights had disappeared; however, a loud, piercing noise could be heard moving south. Two people in the area reported hearing a piercing noise that passed quickly and dogs that became agitated for no apparent reason. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of wheat circles
description: Around July 3, 1993, the owner of a wheat field noticed suspicious markings. The wheat was laid out in large circles connected by straight lines. After an investigation, a landscape architect explained that these were designs he himself created and described the process and method. He was not the one who drew the circles, but the technique he used was the same.

summary: Observation of 2 V-shaped forms composed of luminous spheres.
description: On July 2, 1993, at approximately 10:45 PM, two witnesses observed luminous white orbs forming two V-shaped objects. These objects remained stationary for a few seconds before disappearing at very high speed. These observations were confirmed by the witnesses' spouses. No noise was heard, the weather was clear, and the observation lasted about ten seconds. No other information could be gathered about this phenomenon. This case, previously classified as Class D, was re-examined: observations with similar characteristics were investigated and classified as Class A in August 2009, such as the observation of the Patrouille de France flight: /geipan/actualites/13082009-Des-PAN-en-formation-dans-le-Vaucluse-en-Juillet-2008.html This case is Class A, like the observation of the Patrouille de France flyover.

summary: Observation of a circular shape in horizontal flight and then in ascent
description: On June 29, 1993, at approximately 9:00 AM, two witnesses observed a circular object, five to six meters in diameter, with two tubes hanging from its base in an inverted V shape. The craft flew horizontally and silently at an altitude of about 600 meters, without emitting any smoke or trail. The craft then banked and climbed vertically. One of the witnesses followed the ascent with binoculars until it disappeared into a cloud of Cyrrus clouds, leading to an estimated altitude of approximately 10,000 meters. Military personnel were conducting maneuvers in the vicinity, but the officer present did not observe the phenomenon, which did not appear to be related to the military exercises. After investigation, including inquiries with model aircraft clubs, the phenomenon could not be identified.

summary: Observation of a shape composed of about a hundred points of light
description: On June 27, 1993, at approximately 9:30 PM, a family entertaining guests observed from their terrace a cloud of about one hundred luminous points, each measuring approximately 5 meters by 2.5 meters, without any defined shape. The points moved relative to one another, but the whole formation remained relatively stationary. The witnesses observed the phenomenon with binoculars. After about fifteen minutes, the entire cloud disappeared very quickly. Three witnesses filed a report with the gendarmerie. The observed phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of white lights moving rapidly and describing figures in the sky and on the ground: observation of laser effects.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named CREIL (92) 17.06.1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On June 17, 1993, around 4:00 a.m., a witness observed, first at the foot of his building and then from his car, the rapid movements of two white lights in the sky and on the ground. The UFO described circular patterns moving at very high speed. No unusual noises were heard during the observation, which lasted over 15 minutes. No other witness statements were collected. The description may have seemed stranger during the initial analysis of the case in 1993. With the experience acquired by GEIPAN, there is no doubt today. The description is consistent with laser reflections in the sky, with one or more spots moving back and forth. The witness mentions the presence of clouds, which create a screening effect. The upward beams of the lasers are visible here (not always the case in GEIPAN experiments; sometimes only spots are visible, whereas in other cases only the upward beams are visible, with no final spot in the sky) and are interpreted by the witness as downward beams emitted by the UFO towards the ground. In 1993, laser use was far less widespread than it is today. However, laser tests were identified (see police report) in the vicinity and on the night in question. This element, combined with the well-established characterization of celestial effects, allows us to conclude without hesitation. The testimony is typical of the emotion that an unknown phenomenon can generate in a witness, especially when the illusion arises of an intelligence within the phenomenon that would follow the witness and only appear when the witness is alone, etc. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: laser.

summary: Observations of the evolution of several luminous ovoid shapes in the cloudy sky: probable observations of lasers or "Sky Rose".
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named HERSERANGE (54) 1993, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On the night of May 30-31, 1993, around 2:00 AM, a family was driving home from a family gathering. The mother and her son observed six to eight luminous, ovoid shapes in the overcast sky for approximately five minutes. These shapes move in jumps and circles over a small area, or from right to left, zigzagging through the clouds. Two witness statements were collected; the other family members did not witness the phenomenon. The evidence gathered from the police report leads us to conclude that it was a case of confusion with a Skytracker or SkyRose laser system (see the investigation report). The number, shape, visibility, and behavior of the UFOs support this hypothesis. Furthermore, the day of observation, at the end of the week, is more likely to be used by such a Skytracker, either by a nightclub or at a private party. Laser displays, now frequent and easily recognizable in the testimonies received by GEIPAN, were rarer in 1993. It is not currently possible to investigate the origin of this display at the location or in its vicinity. Nevertheless, we have an observation from this year where the investigation allowed us to trace the activity and highlighted that the equipment producing such effects was sold to nightclubs in France. (See the police report for the observation case ILE BOUCHARD (37) 11.12.1993. ). GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation (but not certain, due to the inability to identify the installation or verify the compatibility of the weather conditions) of a laser or "Sky Rose".

summary: Very long observation of a very bright white object stationary in the sky and very slow disappearance: observation of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named PANTIN (93) 30.05.1993, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On May 30, 1993, at 4:15 a.m., a witness, returning home after an evening out, observed an orange rectangular shape in the sky over Pantin from her balcony. The object, estimated to be about 1 meter in size, appeared stationary for 15 minutes before slowly moving, changing direction, and disappearing over the horizon. The witness observed a flashing red light but heard no sound. Still on his balcony, at 4:30 AM, the same witness observed a second object, this time circular and white, non-dazzling, and stationary. This disc was also estimated to be about 1 meter in size. The witness observed this second phenomenon continuously until 6:00 AM, at which time the UFO disappeared very slowly. There were, in fact, two observations of two distinct UFOs: Initially (see the case of PANTIN (93) 30.05.1993 T1), these were probably the landing lights of an aircraft on a night VFR approach to one of the two Parisian airports located along the witness's line of sight. Aircraft landing lights can indeed be seen from a great distance. For example, on the GEIPAN website, see the case at EZE (06) on May 16, 2014, where such an aircraft was observed at a distance of approximately 36 km from the witness. Another example is at FONTRAILLES (65) on October 31, 2017, where the aircraft's lights were visible and almost stationary during the day from 100 km away for over 10 minutes. The distance prevented the witness from distinguishing anything other than these powerful lights, whose color and brightness are, at night, blended with the red anti-collision light located under the aircraft's fuselage, giving the orange rectangle shape noted by the witness. The eastward direction of movement, the low angular elevation above the horizon, the observation of a flashing red light after the aircraft pivoted on its axis, positioning it facing the runway, the slowness of the movement, and the absence of noise all support the hypothesis. Secondly, the duration of the observation, the slow movement of the UFO across the sky, its circular shape and white color, and its disappearance due to the numerous clouds present that night, all support the hypothesis of confusion with the planet Venus, rising in the east and moving slowly towards the east-southeast while gaining altitude. The witness is probably not accustomed to observing the sky at this late hour of the night and is unfamiliar with these astronomical phenomena. He likely scanned the sky following the attention or concern created by the first observation, which is the primary observation to remember. The consistency is average and benefits primarily from the observation of buildings, which partially compensates for the lack of angular measurements taken by the police during their on-site investigation. This case, PANTIN (93) 30.05.1993 T2, is class A: observation of Venus.

summary: Long observation of a stationary rectangular orange luminous shape followed by slow movement with a change of direction and disappearance over the horizon: probable sighting of an airplane.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named PANTIN (93) 30.05.1993, is part of a set of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On May 30, 1993, at 4:15 a.m., a witness, returning home after an evening out, observed an orange rectangular shape in the sky over Pantin from her balcony. The witness observed a flashing red light but heard no sound. The witness observed this second phenomenon continuously until 6:00 a.m., at which time the UFO disappeared very slowly. There were, in fact, two separate UFO sightings. Initially, these were likely the landing lights of an aircraft on a night VFR approach to one of the two Parisian airports located along the witness's line of sight. Aircraft landing lights can indeed be seen from a great distance. Another example is at FONTRAILLES (65) on October 31, 2017, where the aircraft's lights were visible and almost motionless during the day from 100 km away for over 10 minutes. The witness is probably not accustomed to observing the sky at this late hour of the night and is unfamiliar with these astronomical phenomena. He scanned the sky, likely due to the attention or concern generated by the initial observation, which remains the primary observation. The consistency is moderate and benefits primarily from the observation of buildings, partially compensating for the lack of angular measurements taken by the gendarmes during their on-site investigation. This case, PANTIN (93) 30.05.1993 T1, is classified as Class B: probable aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation in the distance of a bright white disc
description: On May 17, 1993, at approximately 12:15 PM, a witness in his garden observed a bright white disc in the distance, its speed estimated at three or four times that of a commercial airliner. No sound was heard. The witness observed the phenomenon through binoculars for about two minutes. No further information could be gathered about this observation.

summary: Observation from an ultralight aircraft of a sphere moving at high speed
description: On May 16, 1993, at 7:15 PM, two passengers in a microlight aircraft observed a bluish sphere in the distance, rotating on its axis and moving at high speed. The weather and visibility were excellent. The sphere rapidly approached the microlight and crossed its path at high speed. The observation lasted 15 to 20 seconds. Inquiries with civil and military authorities failed to identify the phenomenon, as no aircraft could be identified in this sighting, which was not detected by radar. This phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observation during a journey of a rather elongated bluish shape at the height of the vehicle's headlights; continuous back and forth movement: very likely observation of a disco laser.
description: The publications of GEIPAN (www.geipan.fr) include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to ensure more relevant conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the past few years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named SAINT-GERMAIN-SUR-VIENNE (37) 16.05.1993, is part of a set of cases recently re-examined. This case is also known as CORMERY (37) 1993. On May 16, 1993, between midnight and 1:00 a.m., three people in a vehicle were intrigued by the sight of a phenomenon they had observed several times during their journey. Only one witness reported their observation: the UFO was described as a bluish, insubstantial shape, most often in front of the vehicle at headlight level, at an undetermined distance. The UFO appeared to move from right to left in a continuous back-and-forth motion, always at the same height. The intrigued witnesses did not stop and made a discontinuous observation over a distance of 4 km. Only one testimony was collected. The witnesses most likely observed a disco laser during a Saturday night/Sunday morning (see the investigation report). The described appearance is typical of other observations now well-known to GEIPAN (which was not the case at the time): an elongated shape, illuminated from below by a bluish light, moving back and forth from left to right, an insubstantial and thin object. Although the witness noted that the sky was clear at the observation site, the presence of clouds capable of reflecting a laser was confirmed towards the northern horizon, as a disturbance centered over Great Britain brought the lightning described by the witness. In 1993, disco lasers were certainly few in number, but they did exist. It so happens that a GEIPAN case in the same area, named (ILE BOUCHARD (37) 11.12.1993), proved that disco equipment, known as Sky Rose, had been responsible for observations exhibiting the same typical characteristics as this one. Other GEIPAN observations have shown that the generating equipment could be located several tens of kilometers from the witnesses and that, for the same equipment, the effects in terms of appearance and distance of appearance were variable (atmospheric factors), which of course increases the potential for misinterpretation. Therefore, even if it has not been possible 25 years later to find the generating equipment (or even to prove its absence), the consistency of appearance with what the equipment used at the time could generate allows us to consider the hypothesis as highly probable. The case is class A: highly probable observation of a discotheque laser.

summary: Observations of a red ball moving slowly across the sky: lack of information.
description: On May 8, 1993, at approximately 10:30 PM, three witnesses observed a large, luminous red sphere in the sky. It moved silently and slowly, emitting beams of the same color. After two to three minutes, the sphere quickly disappeared, becoming only a small point of light in the clear sky. No other witness statements were collected, and the police were unable to gather any further details about this phenomenon. The case is classified as Class C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of a beam of light coming from a disco projector
description: At regular intervals, witnesses saw white lights swirling in the sky. The investigation would later show unequivocally that it was an advertising spotlight installed on the roof of a nearby nightclub.

summary: Observation of lights coming from a nightclub's laser cannon.
description: On April 8, 1993, at 11:45 p.m., a police patrol was alerted by several witnesses who reported seeing a bright light above their house. The phenomenon lasted for nearly an hour. An investigation revealed that the laser cannon from a nearby nightclub was the source.

summary: Observation of a stationary green sphere.
description: On April 1, 1993, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness returning home from work observed a very bright green ball, about the size of a traffic light, in the distance. The witness took a route to approach it but found nothing. No further information has been gathered regarding this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a luminous phenomenon in the shape of a train followed by a trail: observation linked to the artificial atmospheric reentry of March 31, 1993 (Cyclone-M rocket).
description: witness at his post at the Sylans toll plaza on the A40 motorway (Neyrolles, Ain department) observed a luminous phenomenon silently passing across the sky for about twenty seconds. This phenomenon, followed by a trail, moved slowly at low altitude through the mountainous landscape. A press article reporting several eyewitness accounts prompted the witness to file a report, but no other witnesses could be found. This case is only moderately consistent (a single witness), but the description of the observed UFO is precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned, although he most likely made a mistake regarding the date of his observation (see the document: investigation notes). The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, speed of movement, trajectory) with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: an artificial atmospheric reentry. Furthermore, this testimony fits perfectly within the context of the mass observation that followed the atmospheric reentry of March 31, 1993 (Cyclone-M rocket). It is not the witness's visual perception that is in question, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (nighttime observation of an unusual astronomical phenomenon, delayed testimony). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to the artificial atmospheric reentry of March 31, 1993.

summary: Observation of a very bright, imposing object in the overcast sky: astronomical observation of the Moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to improve the relevance of the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This particular case was classified as type C in 1993 by SEPRA. During the night of March 1-2, 1993, between 1:15 and 1:20 a.m., a witness observed a luminous phenomenon from his bedroom, which he described as large and resembling "two tears placed end to end." This case is consistent (a single witness, but whose testimony is very detailed), and the description of the observed UAP is very precise. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon, whose light filtered through cloud cover that partially obscured it, giving it strange and variable shapes. Furthermore, the Moon was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness makes no mention of it. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of low-level strangeness is classified as UAP A, observation of the Moon through light clouds.

summary: Brief observation of a flash of white light and a dome-shaped object with 3 luminous circles near the ground: probable observation of ground lights possibly coming from one or more vehicles with high lighting (agricultural, 4x4)
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Among its publications are older cases, originally classified as type D, which are now being re-examined solely to improve the relevance of the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the past few years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This case study, formerly known as LUSIGNAN (86) 1993, is among the cases classified as type D by SEPRA and has recently been re-examined. On February 28, 1993, at approximately 5:30 or 5:45 a.m., a motorist driving on the D150 between Saint-Sauvant (86) and Lusignan (86) observed a very powerful flash of white light on her left and saw a dome-shaped object with three luminous circles. The observation lasted 3 to 4 seconds, the time it took for the witness to continue driving. The following evening, the witness went to the gendarmerie to report the event. Little information has been gathered about this UFO. The witness described the object's elevation above ground as being at most 2 meters, estimated by him from a distance of 300 meters, a distance confirmed by mapping given the position of the woods relative to the road (see the investigation notes). This is a significant distance for assessing ground height. Furthermore, the witness emphasizes the intensity of the UFO's lights; it is possible, even probable, that the witness was unable to distinguish whether or not these lights were attached to the ground. Thus, a key element of strangeness perceived and described by the witness (the UFO being off the ground) cannot be considered valid. Moreover, the gendarmerie's location of the UFO places it at the level of a drivable dirt road. Ultimately, this description strongly suggests the presence of one or more vehicles with high-powered lights (agricultural equipment, a hunting 4x4, etc.), even at this early hour. The witness's visual perception is not the issue. It should be noted that the witness made the observation under poor conditions, while driving and partly through the rearview mirror, and that he did not stop to observe the characteristics of the UFO more precisely, particularly its evolution. These factors lend the testimony a degree of weakness, though still sufficient to validate the hypothesis above. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Ground Lights.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On February 23, 1993, at approximately 10:00 PM, a volunteer firefighter witnessed a very bright streak in the sky while driving on the highway. The streak appeared to burn up in 4 to 5 seconds. The phenomenon described was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of the planet Venus
description: On February 13, 1993, around 7 p.m., and for several days in a row, several witnesses reported seeing an intense, stationary point of light in the sky, the size of a large star. The investigation revealed that the witnesses were likely misled by the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of several luminous spheres the size of a star.
description: On February 1, 1993, around 8:00 PM, and again the following day, three witnesses observed stationary or moving "spheres" of varying colors (green or orange). These spheres, numbering between three and five, were about the size of a star and silent. One of the witnesses reported seeing the phenomenon the previous year. The observation lasted only a few minutes. No further information was available.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On January 18, 1993, at approximately 7:00 PM, two witnesses in a car observed a very rapid flash (2 to 3 seconds) of green light. Ahead of the vehicle, the phenomenon appeared bright red with red "jets." No further information was gathered, but atmospheric reentry is the most likely explanation.

summary: Likely observation of the planet Venus
description: On January 15, 1993, several witnesses observed a very bright, luminous object moving slowly along a straight trajectory. The investigation revealed that it was likely an observation of the planet Venus under unusual circumstances.

summary: Observation of the zigzag movement of a luminous phenomenon: lack of information.
description: In April 2008, a witness reported that during a holiday in the Camargue region in 1993, he and another person observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon. Appearing very quickly, like a shooting star, this phenomenon slowed down, then stopped, zigzagged several times before disappearing vertically at very high speed. Our requests for further information have gone unanswered. This very old observation remains without a precise indication of location or date (January 1st was arbitrarily given). No investigation is possible into an observation that, while not particularly strange, suggests the presence of atmospheric reentry.
